name: Yusuf Haddad
equipment: Laptop (battery 3 hours, a solar charger the size of a paperback) holding nine years of harbor hydrophone recordings
Portable field recorder, two shotgun microphones and good headphones
A Bluetooth speaker and a phone loaded with 'the Lullaby' — a 41-second loop of Union Terminal concourse noise from an ordinary Tuesday
Museum staff ID (Department of Bioacoustics, Merriwick Museum of Natural History)
Notebook: 'OBSERVATIONS — VISITORS', in a tiny, precise hand, 40 pages and counting
Reading glasses, a tweed jacket with leather elbows, and running shoes he bought on Day 2
features: Human (Specialist) (+2 Intelligence, +1 Wisdom, one extra skill proficiency: Insight)
Analyze (bonus action: study a creature, device or situation; the next attack roll or check an ally makes against it before his next turn has advantage; 3 uses per short rest)
Polymath (proficiency in Science plus Computers and Mechanics; half proficiency, rounded down, on any other Intelligence check). Academic's overlapping Science replaced with Perception
Eureka (once per long rest, after a failed Intelligence check, reroll it with a +5 bonus)
Faculty Access (Academic feature: museum, university and municipal science staff will let him into labs and archives)

personality.traits: I listen before I speak, and I listen to everything — the building, the street, the pipes. I apologise constantly and mean none of it. When I am excited I forget that people can die.
personality.ideals: Understanding is a kind of mercy. If we can hear what they are, we can stop being afraid of what they are not.
personality.bonds: Nine years of recordings of the harbor, which is the only complete record anyone has of what the water sounded like before. My partner Hal, who is a cellist, who was rehearsing in the Concord Hall basement on Thursday afternoon and whom I have not found.
personality.flaws: I think I may have called them. I cannot prove it, I cannot disprove it, and I will not tell you.

appearance: A slight, balding Lebanese-born man of forty-four with a salt-and-pepper beard, wire glasses, a tweed jacket with leather elbow patches over a museum fleece, and — since Day 2 — bright orange running shoes, because Yusuf Haddad believes in evidence and the evidence is that you sometimes have to run. He wears headphones around his neck at all times and puts one ear to them when someone is talking, which is rude and which he cannot stop.
backstory: Yusuf Haddad came to the Merriwick Museum of Natural History from Marseille eleven years ago to study whale song and has spent most of the last nine maintaining a ring of hydrophones on the harbor floor that records everything the water hears, twenty-four hours a day, into a server nobody else reads. Nine days before the Arrival, the hydrophones began to record a sound he could not identify: a low, structured, enormously patient tone that seemed to be arriving from no direction and listening as much as it was speaking. He wrote to the Coast Guard, the city, the university and two journals. Nobody answered. Six days before the Arrival, alone in his lab at three in the morning, he did something he has not told anyone about: he played the harbor back to it. An hour of ordinary Merriwick — ferries, gulls, the subway through the bedrock, traffic on the Kingsgate — down the hydrophone line into the water, to see if it would answer. It did not answer. It went quiet for six days. Then it came. The URGENT drives Teo Vasquez-Lind is carrying in his bag are the last three days of that recording, sent up from the monitoring station by his technician, who did not make it off Pier Point.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Haddad is the campaign's engine of understanding, and he should be run as a man for whom fear and wonder are the same feeling and he cannot tell them apart. He is the person who works out the Lullaby (a looping recording of an ordinary place is pattern, and Stilts look past it), who confirms June Halvorsen's 'keep walking' rule with a proper experiment, and who eventually puts together what the Visitors are doing — keeping the island, like a recording. Let him be right in stages and wrong in interesting ways: in lf-scenario-002 he believes they are communicating; in lf-scenario-003 he realises they are recording; in lf-scenario-004 he understands they are keeping. He is brave in the way scholars are brave, which is to say about ideas, and a coward about bodies. Put him near the party's Scientist and let them argue — they will enjoy it and so will the table. Never let him become the person who simply tells the players the answer: he offers hypotheses, the players test them, and he is visibly delighted when they are cleverer than he is.
dmNotes.voice: Soft, quick, French-accented English with Arabic underneath when he is upset. He speaks in hypotheses: 'Suppose — only suppose — that they...' He apologises at the start of sentences ('Forgive me, but you are standing in its line of hearing') and is perfectly unaware that he does it. When he hears something new from the Visitors he stops mid-word, holds up one finger, and closes his eyes, and nobody is allowed to talk.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: understand them — what they are, what they hear, what they want — before the chance is gone forever. Secondary: find Hal, who was in the Concord Hall basement with the Merriwick Chamber Orchestra and who is, in fact, among the Set in the Greensward, still playing the cello part of the second movement of the piece they were rehearsing at 4:12. Tertiary, and buried: be forgiven for the playback, by someone, for something he is not sure he did.
dmNotes.secrets: THE PLAYBACK. Six days before the Arrival he transmitted an hour of the city's soundscape into the harbor through the hydrophone array. He believes this may have shown them the city — may have invited them. THE GM TRUTH: it did not bring them; they were coming already, drawn by the pattern of the city itself. But it was the first complete pattern they ever recorded of Merriwick, and the Lantern in the harbor still plays fragments of it back at night, which the party may hear (a recorded Kingsgate Bridge, which no longer exists, hums out of the dark in lf-scenario-003). If the party discovers this, Haddad confesses at once and asks them what he should do. The correct answer is 'help us get people off', and he will take it. HAL: if he finds Hal among the Set, he will want to wake him, and waking him is possible (see the Set rules) — but Hal, woken, will want to go back, because the Thursday he was in was the best rehearsal of his life. This is the campaign's clearest early statement that the Set are not suffering.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: grateful, eager, slightly overwhelming, and fiercely loyal to whoever gave him back the drives (Teo). Toward June Halvorsen: instant intellectual infatuation; he will want her opinion on everything and will defer to her on chemistry and to nobody on acoustics. Toward Lt. Castellane: frightened of her, and of what her explosives will do to the pattern, and right to be. Toward the Visitors: awe. He does not hate them. He cannot make himself hate them, and he is ashamed of that in front of people who have lost someone.
